messages:
IncidentBot: Pager alert — sev2: Runtime serving error spike in us-west-2 (increased 5xx + latency)
IncidentBot: Metric: kvcache_miss_rate from 2% -> 42% in last 5m; continuous_batching rejections up 3.8x
Sam: seeing tool/function call errors in the logs, structured outputs with top-level arrays seem to blow up batching paths
Sam: example log: `ERROR batch_worker: break_on_structured_output: got array, flushing batch (req_id=abc-123)`
Lee: ugh, that lines up with the new schema changes from yesterday's model onboarding PR — funcalls returning [ {..}, {..} ] instead of { "items": [...] }
Maya: customers impacted? any high-traffic tenants?
Jordan: yes — enterprise-acme and billing-proxy spiking latency to 800ms p95; 5xx rate ~12% for them. Other small tenants seeing transient slowdowns
Sam: root cause hypothesis: continuous batching expects deterministic structured tokens to build KV cache keys; arrays are causing tokenization variance and frequent kv cache misses, which collapses batching efficiency and amplifies CPU/GPU pressure
Lee: quick mitigation: throttle funcall/structured-output paths at router level to fall back to sync single-request mode for schema-variant models
Maya: agree. Can we add a temporary predicate: if response contains '[' at start of structured token stream, bypass batching? risky but fast
Jordan: I'll push a router rule in a minute. ETA ~3m. Will set rule to 10rps per model to drain backlog
Oncall-Infra: heads up — throttling will increase per-token cost but should reduce 5xx and lower tail latency. Notifying CS for impacted customers now
Sam: running `curl -s -XPOST https://control-plane/api/v1/route/rules -d '{"model":"open-struct-v2","rule":"throttle_funcall:10"}'` (dry run)
Sam: applying rule now: `kubectl exec -n redwood router-1 -- /bin/sh -c \"redwoodctl route apply --json /tmp/throttle.json\"`
Lee: metrics after 2m: kvcache_miss_rate dropping 42% -> 18%, continuous_batch_rejects down 70%
Maya: 5xx for enterprise-acme down to 3% and p95 latency back to ~320ms. Good
Jordan: we should still deploy a patch to conservative-serialize structured outputs so they don't change tokenization mid-stream. Adding to eng-runtime backlog but need hotfix ASAP
Sam: creating quick hotfix branch to normalize funcall outputs to an object wrapper: `{ "items": <original> }` before being emitted to router. If we can land and rollout fast we can remove throttles
Lee: do not restart serving processes. We'll do a config-only rollout via runtime feature flag toggle. Patch ready: `rev-ff1c9`
Jordan: rolling out rev-ff1c9 to canary group (10% of capacity) now. Observability hooks enabled
Maya: after canary 5m: no regressions, kvcache hit improved on canary hosts, rollback not needed
Sam: scaling canary to 50% then 100% over next 10m. Keeping throttles until 100% confirmed
Oncall-Infra: I'll draft status update for customers and join handoff notes. Paging suppressed for now but still monitoring 15m cadence
Lee: handoff to night oncall at 1965432345 — leaving runbook: throttles applied, rev-ff1c9 deployed, monitor kvcache_miss_rate and continuous_batch_rejects, watch for any funcall schema regressions.
Maya: thanks — tagging @Oncall-Infra and @Jordan for night follow-up. :thumbsup:
IncidentBot: Incident update: mitigation applied — throttles + runtime hotfix. Severity downgraded to sev3. Next update at +30m or on any regression
